**Considering button functionalities**

I'm thinking about button semantics, particularly how selected versus auto-clear works. There's a mix of unit groups; selected levels should persist when switching subunits and badges count across all levels. It's important to note that switching units clears selection, which is documented. The Quick Select modal allows for selecting all or random sets in units. Also, there's a standalone Random 10 button that selects sets while preserving level order. I should mention the integration of Kanji and Vocabulary, especially regarding the two modes.

I couldn’t retrieve issue #28524 from GitHub here, so this explanation uses the concerns you listed and the changes in the code.

- **Quick Select and Random 10 are back.** In [LevelSetCards.tsx](C:/Users/nishi/Projects/kana-dojo/shared/ui-composite/Menu/LevelSetCards.tsx), users can open Quick Select for bulk choices or pick 10 random levels with one click. This avoids having to select many levels manually.
- **Selections can span level groups.** In [UnitSelector.tsx](C:/Users/nishi/Projects/kana-dojo/shared/ui-composite/Menu/UnitSelector.tsx), switching between groups no longer clears picked levels. A count on each group tab shows what’s selected elsewhere, and bulk actions apply to the whole unit. That makes it possible to train a mix of levels without losing track of any.
- **Bulk selection stays consistent.** Quick Select and Random 10 now replace the selection, keeping the listed levels and the actual training items in sync. Previously, actions that toggled items could leave those out of step.
- **Start buttons do what their labels imply.** In [AutoLearningButton.tsx](C:/Users/nishi/Projects/kana-dojo/shared/ui-composite/Menu/AutoLearningButton.tsx), the button indicates when it will start selected levels and how many. The Kanji and Vocabulary pages route to selected-level training when levels are picked, and use auto-learning when they aren’t ([Kanji](C:/Users/nishi/Projects/kana-dojo/features/Kanji/components/index.tsx), [Vocabulary](C:/Users/nishi/Projects/kana-dojo/features/Vocabulary/components/index.tsx)). The bottom action bar also starts the current selection directly ([TrainingActionBar.tsx](C:/Users/nishi/Projects/kana-dojo/shared/ui-composite/Menu/TrainingActionBar.tsx)).

**Overall:** the changes restore quick ways to choose levels, let users combine groups without hidden selections, and make starting training less ambiguous.

response.value:
Thanks—that clarifies the motivation. The issue wasn’t just asking for more selection options: the new selector made **Play feel unpredictable** and made choosing specific levels take too many clicks. The changes address those frustrations:

- **Quick Select is back:** users can choose levels in bulk instead of selecting them one by one. See [LevelSetCards.tsx](C:/Users/nishi/Projects/kana-dojo/shared/ui-composite/Menu/LevelSetCards.tsx).
- **Random 10 is back:** users can quickly start a varied session of ten levels, the option the issue specifically said they liked. It picks levels from the current unit.
- **Groups can be mixed:** switching between level groups keeps the user’s picks, so they can build one session from levels across groups. Counts on the group tabs show selections that aren’t currently visible. See [UnitSelector.tsx](C:/Users/nishi/Projects/kana-dojo/shared/ui-composite/Menu/UnitSelector.tsx).
- **Start buttons are clearer:** when levels are selected, the button says how many and starts those levels; when none are selected, it continues with auto-learning. This helps prevent “Play” from appearing to choose something arbitrary. See [AutoLearningButton.tsx](C:/Users/nishi/Projects/kana-dojo/shared/ui-composite/Menu/AutoLearningButton.tsx), [Kanji](C:/Users/nishi/Projects/kana-dojo/features/Kanji/components/index.tsx), and [Vocabulary](C:/Users/nishi/Projects/kana-dojo/features/Vocabulary/components/index.tsx).

In short, this brings back the fast, predictable ways to start a session that the issue’s author missed, while making custom selections easier to manage.
